description:
The Two-Minute Rule — explained in 60 seconds.

Shrink every habit to under two minutes. The goal isn't the result — it's becoming the kind of person who starts.

What actually happens in your brain: Habits fail at the startup cost, not the workload. A 'read one page' habit keeps the identity alive; volume can grow later.

Try it today: 'Read before bed' fails. 'Read ONE page' works — and pages stack. Start stupidly small tonight.

You probably believe this: BIG GOALS NEED BIG STARTS. But that's not the full story.
Shrink every habit to under two minutes. The goal isn't the result, it's becoming the kind of person who starts. Here's what's happening: Habits fail at the startup cost, not the workload.
Behavioral research on habit formation Lally and colleagues, 2010: automaticity depends on repetition consistency far more than intensity.
